facts.statement: Jingshanosaurus lived in China during the Early Jurassic period, specifically between 201.4 and 196.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Jingshanosaurus (meaning "Jingshan lizard") is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the early Jurassic period (201.4 to 196.5 million years ago, Hettangian age) of China.

facts.statement: Fossils of Jingshanosaurus were discovered near the town of Jingshan in Yunnan Province, China, giving the animal its name.
facts.quote: Its fossils, a nearly complete skeleton including the skull, were found near the town of Jingshan ("Golden Hill"), Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, China, from which the name derives.

facts.statement: The genus was first formally described in 1995 by Zhang and Yang.
facts.quote: First described in 1995, the type species is J. xinwaensis, formalized by Zhang and Yang.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton including the skull has been found, and Jingshanosaurus is considered the last prosauropod to live on Earth.
facts.quote: A complete skeleton and skull of Jingshanosaurus xinwaensis have been found and is considered the last prosauropods to live on earth.

facts.statement: Adult Jingshanosaurus reached a length of 5 meters and weighed approximately 4.3 tons.
facts.quote: Its maximum weight was around 4.3 t with an adult femur length of 845 mm. The genus grew up to 5 m long.

facts.statement: Some sources estimate Jingshanosaurus reached a length of about 10 meters and a height of 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Jingshanosaurus medía aproximadamente 10 metros de largo y 2,5 de alto.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Jingshanosaurus may have had an omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Se cree que pudo presentar una dieta omnívora.

facts.statement: Jingshanosaurus is classified within the suborder Prosauropoda.
Jingshanosaurus belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
In 2004, paleontologists Peter Galton and Paul Upchurch grouped Jingshanosaurus into the clade Plateosauria.
facts.quote: En el 2004, el Jingshanosaurus fue agrupado por Peter Galton y Paul Upchurch en el clado Plateosauria.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Jingshanosaurus is a distinct genus or merely a large specimen of Yunnanosaurus, which would make it a junior synonym.
facts.quote: In fact, Dong Zhiming considered Jingshanosaurus possibly a large specimen of Yunnanosaurus. If true, this would make Jingshanosaurus a junior synonym of Yunnanosaurus.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Jingshanosaurus spans from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)
